title: PubMatrixR with Ligand Receptors
text: WNT ligands receptors pair neatly. given ligand can bind several receptors, literature reflects : ligand-receptor combinations turn paper paper, others almost never. vignette counts co-occurrences. compares 19 WNT ligands 15 receptors (FZD1-10, LRP5/6, ROR1/2, RYK), gives 15x19 grid PubMed counts. Bear mind numbers actually measure: often two gene symbols appear record, whether paper found interact.
code: library(PubMatrixR) library(knitr) library(kableExtra) library(dplyr) library(pheatmap) library(ggplot2) A <- c(   "WNT1", "WNT2", "WNT2B", "WNT3", "WNT3A", "WNT4", "WNT5A", "WNT5B",   "WNT6", "WNT7A", "WNT7B", "WNT8A", "WNT8B", "WNT9A", "WNT9B",   "WNT10A", "WNT10B", "WNT11", "WNT16" )  B <- c(   "FZD1", "FZD2", "FZD3", "FZD4", "FZD5", "FZD6", "FZD7",   "FZD8", "FZD9", "FZD10", "LRP5", "LRP6", "ROR1", "ROR2", "RYK" )

title: PubMatrixR with Ligand Receptors
text: better performance higher rate limits, recommend obtaining NCBI API key: Without API key: 3 requests per second API key: 10 requests per second obtain free NCBI API key, visit: https://support.nlm.nih.gov/kbArticle/?pn=KA-05317 API key, pass PubMatrix() like : live rendering, vignette picks key NCBI_API_KEY environment variable instead hardcoding , key stored file:
code: result <- PubMatrix(   A = A,   B = B,   API.key = "your_api_key_here",   Database = "pubmed" ) NCBI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here PUBMATRIX_LIVE_VIGNETTE=true \   Rscript -e 'pkgdown::build_site()' current_year <- as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")) result <- PubMatrix(   A = A,   B = B,   API.key = ncbi_api_key,   Database = "pubmed",   daterange = c(1990, current_year),   outfile = "pubmatrix_result" ) # Offline deterministic example used for vignette rendering/package checks. result <- outer(seq_along(B), seq_along(A), function(i, j) {   10 + (i * 5) + (j * 4) + ((i + j) %% 5) * 2 + ((i * j) %% 6) }) result <- as.data.frame(result, check.names = FALSE) colnames(result) <- A rownames(result) <- B

what: Which genes get the most attention
title: PubMatrixR with Ligand Receptors
text: looking pairs, check totals. bar charts sum gene’s row column colour strongest partner list, can see receptor dominates given ligand’s literature way round.
code: # Create data frame for List A genes (rows) colored by List B genes (columns) a_genes_data <- data.frame(   gene = rownames(result),   total_pubs = rowSums(result),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  # Add color coding based on max overlap with B genes a_genes_data$max_b_gene <- apply(result, 1, function(x) colnames(result)[which.max(x)]) a_genes_data$max_overlap <- apply(result, 1, max)  # Create data frame for List B genes (columns) colored by List A genes (rows) b_genes_data <- data.frame(   gene = colnames(result),   total_pubs = colSums(result),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  # Add color coding based on max overlap with A genes b_genes_data$max_a_gene <- apply(result, 2, function(x) rownames(result)[which.max(x)]) b_genes_data$max_overlap <- apply(result, 2, max)  # Plot A genes colored by their strongest B gene partner p1 <- ggplot(a_genes_data, aes(x = reorder(gene, total_pubs), y = total_pubs, fill = max_b_gene)) +   geom_bar(stat = "identity") +   coord_flip() +   labs(     title = "List A Genes by Publication Count",     subtitle = "Colored by strongest List B gene partner",     x = "Genes (List A)",     y = "Total Publications",     fill = "Strongest B Partner"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom") +   scale_fill_viridis_d()   # Plot B genes colored by their strongest A gene partner p2 <- ggplot(b_genes_data, aes(x = reorder(gene, total_pubs), y = total_pubs, fill = max_a_gene)) +   geom_bar(stat = "identity") +   coord_flip() +   labs(     title = "List B Genes by Publication Count",     subtitle = "Colored by strongest List A gene partner",     x = "Genes (List B)",     y = "Total Publications",     fill = "Strongest A Partner"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom") +   scale_fill_viridis_d()   print(p1) print(p2)

what: Making the gene lists from MSigDB
title: PubMatrixR: Literature Co-occurrence Analysis
text: example, ’ll extract genes related WNT signaling obesity MSigDB database: msigdf optional required build vignette. example shown reference executed package checks.
code: # Extract WNT-related genes A <- msigdf::msigdf.human %>%   dplyr::filter(grepl(geneset, pattern = "wnt", ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%   dplyr::pull(symbol) %>%   unique()  # Extract obesity-related genes B <- msigdf::msigdf.human %>%   dplyr::filter(grepl(geneset, pattern = "obesity", ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%   dplyr::pull(symbol) %>%   unique()  # Sample genes for demonstration (making them equal in length) A <- sample(A, 10, replace = FALSE) B <- sample(B, 10, replace = FALSE)

text: Let’s first examine genes highest publication counts:
code: # Create data frame for List A genes (rows) colored by List B genes (columns) a_genes_data <- data.frame(   gene = rownames(result),   total_pubs = rowSums(result),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  # Add color coding based on max overlap with B genes a_genes_data$max_b_gene <- apply(result, 1, function(x) colnames(result)[which.max(x)]) a_genes_data$max_overlap <- apply(result, 1, max)  # Create data frame for List B genes (columns) colored by List A genes (rows) b_genes_data <- data.frame(   gene = colnames(result),   total_pubs = colSums(result),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  # Add color coding based on max overlap with A genes b_genes_data$max_a_gene <- apply(result, 2, function(x) rownames(result)[which.max(x)]) b_genes_data$max_overlap <- apply(result, 2, max)  bar_plot_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   theme(     plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),     plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),     axis.title = element_text(size = 11),     axis.text = element_text(size = 10),     panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),     legend.position = "bottom",     legend.title = element_text(size = 10),     legend.text = element_text(size = 9),     legend.box = "vertical"   )  n_fill_a <- length(unique(a_genes_data$max_b_gene)) n_fill_b <- length(unique(b_genes_data$max_a_gene))  # Plot A genes colored by their strongest B gene partner p1 <- ggplot(a_genes_data, aes(x = reorder(gene, total_pubs), y = total_pubs, fill = max_b_gene)) +   geom_col(width = 0.75) +   coord_flip() +   labs(     title = "List A Genes by Publication Count",     subtitle = "Colored by strongest List B partner",     x = "Genes (List A)",     y = "Total Publications",     fill = "Strongest B Partner"   ) +   scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D", end = 0.9) +   guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = max(1, ceiling(n_fill_a / 4)), byrow = TRUE)) +   bar_plot_theme   # Plot B genes colored by their strongest A gene partner p2 <- ggplot(b_genes_data, aes(x = reorder(gene, total_pubs), y = total_pubs, fill = max_a_gene)) +   geom_col(width = 0.75) +   coord_flip() +   labs(     title = "List B Genes by Publication Count",     subtitle = "Colored by strongest List A partner",     x = "Genes (List B)",     y = "Total Publications",     fill = "Strongest A Partner"   ) +   scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D", end = 0.9) +   guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = max(1, ceiling(n_fill_b / 4)), byrow = TRUE)) +   bar_plot_theme   print(p1) print(p2)

title: PubMed Pairwise Co-Occurrence Matrix Construction and Visualization
text: PubMatrixR R package performs systematic literature searches PubMed PMC databases using pairwise combinations search terms. creates co-occurrence matrices showing number publications mention terms two different sets, enabling researchers explore relationships genes, diseases, pathways, biomedical concepts. repository maintains extends original PubMatrixR package improved validation, offline-safe tests/vignettes, heatmap helpers.

text: Examples vignettes avoid live web queries package checks. function performs live requests 'NCBI' may fail internet connectivity service unavailable. Terms trimmed surrounding whitespace, duplicate terms within `` within `B` rejected. reading `file`, blank lines either side `#` separator ignored. Requests paced respect 'NCBI' rate limits (3 requests per second without API key, 10 one). Two options tune request behaviour: `PubMatrixR.n_tries` - number attempts per query giving     (default `3`). Failed attempts back exponentially. `PubMatrixR.min_interval` - seconds wait requests     (default `0.34` without API key, `0.11` one). Set `0`     disable pacing.

Default "PubMatrix Co-occurrence Heatmap" cluster_rows Logical value determining rows clustered using Euclidean distance. Default TRUE cluster_cols Logical value determining columns clustered using Euclidean distance. Default TRUE show_numbers Logical value determining overlap percentage values displayed cells. Default TRUE color_palette Color palette heatmap. Default uses red gradient color scale filename Optional filename save heatmap. NULL, displays plot width Width saved plot inches. Default 10 height Height saved plot inches. Default 8 cellwidth Optional numeric cell width pheatmap (pixels). Default `NA` lets pheatmap auto-size. cellheight Optional numeric cell height pheatmap (pixels). Default `NA` lets pheatmap auto-size. scale_font Logical value determining font size scale cell size. title: Create a formatted heatmap from PubMatrix results — plot_pubmatrix_heatmap
text: Rows columns clustered Euclidean distance. NA values input matrix converted 0 calculation. `values` argument controls cell shows: `"raw"` (default) - co-occurrence counts . `"row_pct"` - count percentage row total, useful     comparing one row's attention distributed across columns. `"relative"` - `count / (row_total + col_total - count) * 100`,     totals sums supplied matrix. Note `"relative"` **** Jaccard index **comparable across runs**. totals sums whichever partner terms happen matrix, marginal publication counts term, adding unrelated term changes value reported every existing cell. true Jaccard index require single-term counts, [PubMatrix()] fetch. Use compare cells within one fixed matrix.

title: Create a formatted heatmap from PubMatrix results — plot_pubmatrix_heatmap
code: # Create a small test matrix test_matrix <- matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 4), nrow = 2, ncol = 2) rownames(test_matrix) <- c("Gene1", "Gene2") colnames(test_matrix) <- c("GeneA", "GeneB")  # Create heatmap using the helper (plots the raw counts by default) plot_pubmatrix_heatmap(test_matrix, title = "Test Heatmap")   # Percentage views are available too: plot_pubmatrix_heatmap(test_matrix, values = "row_pct", title = "Row %")   # Equivalent using pheatmap directly: pheatmap::pheatmap(   test_matrix,   main = "Test Heatmap (pheatmap)",   color = colorRampPalette(c("#fee5d9", "#cb181d"))(100),   display_numbers = TRUE,   fontsize = 16,   fontsize_number = 14,   border_color = "lightgray",   show_rownames = TRUE,   show_colnames = TRUE )
